name: Phase-sequence indicator
summary: Instrument that shows whether three-phase supply rotation is positive or reversed before motors are run or sources paralleled.
description: A phase-sequence indicator connects to all three phases and shows whether rotation is L1-L2-L3 or reversed. It is used when commissioning motors, generators and supply changes, because wrong rotation reverses motors and prevents correct paralleling.

The instrument gives a check at one moment and does not protect anything on its own. If permanent protection against reversed rotation is needed, a phase-sequence monitoring relay with contacts must be shown instead of, or as well as, the indicator.
readingNotes: Confirm all three phases are connected in the stated order.
Check whether a protective relay is also required.
distinction: A phase-sequence indicator only displays rotation; a phase monitoring relay acts on incorrect rotation or loss of phase.
